comment: The one assignment of wire tags: for each listed family, the number every active constructor
carries in the canonical bytes, and the numbers retired constructors held.
Readers: the generator of Lean codecs (tools/Effect4Gen/Main.lean) and its projection guard
(tools/Effect4Gen/Check.lean), the OCaml codec and the golden bytes (src/OCaml5/Eff/World.lean,
src/OCaml5/Tools/EffGen.lean), the TypeScript writer (tools/Tools/TsGen.lean), the wire manifest
(src/OCaml5/Tools/EffWire.lean) and the compatibility check (scripts/lib/compatibility.py).
The Lean readers share one loader, tools/Tools/WireTags.lean.
Rules every reader enforces. The active names of a listed family are exactly its declared
constructors. Inside one family no tag and no name appears twice across active and retired.
A retired name is not a declared constructor. A structure is never listed: it is constructor 0.
A family that is not listed carries its declaration positions and has no retired tag; every
inductive family of the program world (tools/Tools/ProgramStructure.lean) must be listed.
A wire tag is not a compiled constructor position. The runtime layout checks
(tools/Conform/Source/Description.lean, scripts/lib/program_structure.py) keep reading the
declaration itself.
To add a constructor: give it the next tag above every active and retired tag of its family.
To retire one: move its row from active to retired, tag unchanged. A tag is never given twice.
History. Before this file the tag was the declaration position. `Eff.choose` held 23 and was
removed at 75d75fdb; `provideLayer`, `service` and `provideService` moved down from 24, 25, 26
to 23, 24, 25. That one reuse is named in the compatibility policy
(Test/fixtures/baseline/66ee4657-supplement-v1.policy.json) and is why `choose` has no
retired row here.
